messages:
maria: quick question — we're seeing mixed score shapes from clients hitting /rerank (some send raw logits, some probability floats). should we standardize on a 0-1 `normalized_score` and make routing/quota layers depend on that?
aj: +1 for normalized 0-1, makes routing thresholds sane. but we should also carry a small enum `score_type` so we know how it was derived (prob, logit, distance).
sam: breaking change is scary. can we accept both and add server-side normalization for a transition period? add a response header `X-Rerank-Score-Version: v2` when we return normalized scores.
leo: telemetry note: console wants a heatmap of score distribution per model. if we normalize server-side we need to preserve original provenance for debugging/regressions. add `raw_score` optional field.
natalie: for quota counting: do we charge per-candidate or per-scored-token? current billing expects "score units" = candidates * model_weight. If normalized scores are 0-1 we could add cost-savings for low-score short-circuits (e.g., drop below 0.05). risky but could lower costs.
aj: important: routing policies use score to pick downstream model variants for explain/coverage. if we normalize, define buckets: [0-0.2)=low, [0.2-0.6)=medium, [0.6-1]=high. routing rules can then map buckets to `cheap-model`, `default`, `hedged-model`.
maria: example payload i'm picturing:```json
{
  "candidates": [{"id":"u1","text":"..."}],
  "scores": [{"id":"u1","normalized_score":0.87,"raw_score":2.3,"score_type":"logit"}]
}
```
sam: that shape is fine. add optional `score_bucket` as hint so we avoid recomputing on the router: "\"score_bucket\":\"high\"". router still verifies bucket though.
leo: console UX: add a per-route toggle to surface the chosen bucket thresholds and live percent falling into each bucket. also per-model percentile lines so SRE can see drift.
natalie: rollout plan idea: default to passthrough (accept both), emit warnings in logs when raw non-normalized scores seen, then enable normalization flag behind feature flag, then flip default after 2 weeks.
aj: compatibility: client SDKs should map `score`->`normalized_score` when `score_type` is prob. for logits we need stable sigmoid mapping with model-level calibration metadata. we should store calibration params per-model.
maria: question for infra — how will this affect quota math? if we add `score_bucket` shortcuts, quota still counts candidates, right? not changing units?
infra-bot: created infra ticket INFRA-2241 to surface quota impact and console metrics. https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-2241
sam: operational fallback: if normalization fails (missing calibration metadata), router should treat as `medium` bucket and route to `default` model, log event with trace id.
leo: telemetry event fields proposal: `rerank.score.raw_score`, `rerank.score.normalized`, `rerank.score.bucket`, `rerank.model.routed`, `rerank.client.sdk_version`. will feed console.
aj: security note: don't accept arbitrary `raw_score` without provenance — require `signing_token` if client submits precomputed scores for routing decisions. otherwise potential poisoning.
maria: thanks all. next steps: (1) RFC draft with schema + backward compat plan (2) infra ticket for quota calc (3) console mockups for bucket view. i'll draft RFC and ping for reviews.
infra-bot: RFC created at https://redwood.internal/rfcs/rerank-score-v2 — review requested from @aj @sam @leo
